catalogue.note: Read from Figma at real size (375×800, nothing scaled): auto-layout frames are flex with Figma’s direction, gap, padding and alignment, everything else sits at its Figma offset, and all 31 boxes land on Figma’s to 0.05px. Square-cornered: the frame’s own 16px corners are left off and the diff leaves the four corners out (308 pixels). Nothing overlaps on this screen. The bottom button block (“button action input”) is the last 104px of the frame, with no home indicator under it; its own 16px top corners are kept. Both pickers have a 1px #B9B9BB inside stroke, drawn as an inset shadow. The hidden “Fee” row is absent. Icons (bank logo, edit, back chevron) are Figma’s SVG export. The iOS status bar is Figma’s SVG export: the time (SF Pro Text Semibold 17) as Figma’s outline, signal, wifi and battery as its vectors. Baselines: Figma rounds a line’s baseline to a whole pixel where Chrome rounds ascent and descent apart; the 23px title and the 19px nav title sit 1px lower than Chrome puts them, and the three 18px bold lines (two pickers, Continue) land on a half pixel that Figma draws on the row above (−0.5px). The offsets are Figma’s baseline (its render bounds plus the glyph height from the font file) minus Chrome’s, not fitted to the picture. What is left in the diff is glyph and curve edges: Figma’s rasteriser against Chrome’s. Flat fills match exactly.
